sops.title: IT Security Incident Handling & Recovery Procedure

blocks.text: This SOP outlines the Incident Response Procedure (IRP) for managing breaches of confidential information at Permeshwar Creations Pvt. Ltd.. The purpose is to provide clear instructions for detecting, responding to, and minimizing the impact of information security breaches to prevent further damage, protect sensitive data, and reassure affected parties.

This SOP applies to all employees, contractors, and third-party service providers who have access to confidential information related to Permeshwar Creations Pvt. Ltd. It covers breaches involving data loss, unauthorized access, disclosure of confidential information, or any other information security incidents.

rows: Rishita Fashion
Plot no. 1102, Phase III, GIDC, Vapi, Valsad, Gujarat.
PK Enterprises
C-19, Hoisery Complex, Phase II, Noida, U.P- 201301, India.

substeps.text: Monitoring Systems: All company systems handling confidential information should be monitored regularly for any suspicious activity, unauthorized access, or other indications of a breach.

Reporting Channels: Employees must report any suspicious activity or potential breaches to the Information Security Officer (ISO) immediately. The ISO can be contacted via email at iso@permeshwarcreations.com or by phone at 91-022-28226245.
Automated Alerts: Systems are equipped with automated alerts to notify the ISO of unusual access patterns, failed login attempts, or other triggers indicating a potential breach.
Assessment: Upon detecting or receiving a report of a potential breach, the ISO will assess the situation to determine the scope, severity, and type of incident.

Classification: Incidents will be classified into one of the following categories: Low Severity: Minor incidents with no significant impact on confidential information. Medium Severity: Incidents involving some exposure of confidential information, with limited potential for harm. High Severity: Major breaches where sensitive data is exposed, and there is a significant risk to business operations, clients, or other stakeholders.

Immediate Action: Once a breach is confirmed, the Information Security Officer will activate the incident response team to take immediate steps to contain the breach, preventing further unauthorized access or data loss.
System Isolation: In the event of an ongoing breach, affected systems will be temporarily isolated from the network to stop further damage.
Access Revocation: If necessary, user accounts or credentials involved in the breach will be revoked or reset to prevent further exploitation.
Data Backup: Ensure all critical data is backed up to avoid data loss or corruption during the containment process.
Internal Notification: Relevant internal stakeholders, including department heads, IT personnel, and legal teams, will be notified of the breach and the steps being taken.

External Notification: In cases where client data or third-party information is affected, external parties will be notified promptly. Notifications will include: A description of the breach and the data involved. Steps being taken to mitigate the impact and prevent future incidents. Contact information for further inquiries:

Root Cause Analysis: The incident response team will conduct a full investigation to determine the root cause of the breach. This includes identifying vulnerabilities in the system, human errors, or any malicious activities.
Documentation: All details of the breach, including timelines, actions taken, and communication with affected parties, will be thoroughly documented.
Forensic Analysis: If needed, forensic experts will be engaged to conduct in-depth analysis of the breach, particularly for high-severity incidents.
System Restoration: After containing the breach, the IT team will work to restore affected systems and ensure their security before bringing them back online.
Patch and Fix Vulnerabilities: Vulnerabilities identified during the investigation will be patched or mitigated to prevent similar breaches in the future.
User Training: Employees involved in the breach or who could prevent future breaches may be required to undergo additional security training.

Customer Communication: Affected customers or third parties will receive clear communication on the status of the breach, the measures being taken to secure their data, and steps they can take to protect themselves.
Follow-Up Support: The company will provide ongoing support to affected parties to address concerns, including offering credit monitoring or other services if necessary.
Debriefing: Once the incident has been fully managed, a post-incident review will be conducted by the Information Security Officer and the response team to evaluate the effectiveness of the response.
Lessons Learned: The review will focus on identifying lessons learned from the breach and areas for improvement in the company's security infrastructure and incident response plan.
System and Policy Enhancements: Based on the post-incident review, the company will update its security policies, systems, and procedures to strengthen defenses against future breaches.
Incident Response Plan Updates: The IRP will be revised as needed to incorporate the new findings and ensure a more effective response in future incidents.
Security Awareness Training: Employees will undergo regular security awareness training, with additional emphasis on lessons learned from recent incidents.

responsibilities: Oversees the detection, response, and mitigation of information security breaches.
Coordinates communication with affected parties and stakeholders.
Leads the post-incident review and ensures proper documentation.
Activated in the event of a confirmed breach.

Ensures that systems are monitored and alerts are in place for detecting breaches.

Provides guidance on regulatory requirements related to breaches of confidential information.

narrative.text:
Incident Tracking: All breaches, regardless of severity, will be logged in the company's incident tracking system. This log will include key details such as the type of breach, impacted data, and actions taken.
Regular Audits: The ISO will conduct regular audits of the incident response process to ensure the procedures are followed, and improvements are identified.

rows.definition: These include gifts, travel expenses, or other benefits that could create a conflict of interest or influence business decisions. Examples include non-routine travel, gifts exceeding monetary thresholds, or any benefit that may appear to compromise company integrity.
Designated individuals or departments responsible for reviewing and approving sensitive transactions. These may include department heads, senior management, or the executive committee.

body.text: Identification:

All sensitive transactions, such as gifts exceeding ₹5,000 or travel expenses above ₹25,000, must be identified and documented.
Thresholds: Any gift or benefit valued over ₹5,000 or travel expenses over ₹25,000 requires specific approval.
Documentation:
A Sensitive Transaction Request Form must be completed for each transaction, which includes the following:

Name of the recipient
Description of the transaction (gift, travel, etc.)
Monetary value
Purpose of the transaction
Date and location
Justification for the transaction and any supporting documentation (e.g., travel itineraries, invoices).

Submit the completed Sensitive Transaction Request Form to the immediate supervisor or department head for an initial review.
The supervisor will evaluate the transaction for compliance with company policies and potential conflicts of interest.

Approval Authorities:
Transactions requiring approval should be submitted to the following authorities based on the value.
Gifts:
Above ₹5,000: Department Head
Above ₹10,000: Senior Management
Travel Expenses:
Above ₹25,000: Senior Management
Above ₹50,000: Executive Committee

Approval Procedure:
The approving authority will review the documentation and justification provided. They may request additional information if needed.
Approval or rejection of the transaction must be documented in writing, including reasons for approval or denial.

Processing:
Once approved, process the transaction according to company procedures. Ensure that all documentation is complete and accurate.
For travel-related expenses, book travel in accordance with Permeshwar Creations’ travel policies.
Recording:
Maintain a record of all sensitive transactions, including approvals, supporting documentation, and any related correspondence.
Records should be retained for a minimum of 5 years and made available for audit or review as needed.

Post-Transaction Review:
Conduct annual reviews of sensitive transactions to ensure compliance with policies and identify any potential issues or patterns.
Review findings should be documented and reported to the relevant authorities for further action if required.

sops.title: Data Access Controls: Best Practices and Challenges

blocks.text: This SOP establishes the necessary steps and controls to protect third-party data from unauthorized access or disclosure and outlines the measures for gaining stakeholder consent regarding the processing, sharing, and retention of confidential information. The aim is to safeguard customer and client data while ensuring compliance with data protection regulations and building trust with stakeholders.

This SOP applies to all employees, contractors, and third-party service providers who handle customer, client, or other stakeholder data for Permeshwar Creations Pvt. Ltd. It ensures secure data management and transparency in processing and storage.

sections.title: Key measures to safeguard third-party data

substeps.text: Restricted Areas: Confidential data will only be stored in restricted areas such as secure server rooms, vaults, or locked file cabinets that can only be accessed by authorized personnel.

Employee Access Control: Employees who require access to sensitive data must request clearance from the Information Security Officer (ISO). Access will be granted only based on the principle of least privilege, ensuring that employees only access the data necessary for their role.

Physical Security: Access to premises where sensitive data is stored will be restricted via electronic access cards, biometric authentication, or PIN codes. Visitors and third-party contractors must be logged in and accompanied at all times when accessing these areas.
Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): Digital access to sensitive customer and client data will be managed through role-based access control (RBAC), limiting access to specific users based on job roles.

Two-Factor Authentication (2FA): All systems containing confidential data will require two-factor authentication to ensure secure login. Employees will authenticate via both password and a secondary security measure (e.g., mobile app verification, hardware tokens).

Data Encryption: All confidential data in transit (e.g., email, file transfer) and at rest (e.g., databases, hard drives) must be encrypted using industry-standard encryption protocols such as AES-256.

Audit Logs: All access to customer data will be logged in an audit trail that tracks the time, user, and data accessed. Logs will be regularly reviewed by the IT security team to detect unauthorized or unusual access patterns.

Vendor Contracts: Third-party vendors who handle sensitive customer data will be required to sign Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs) and will undergo a vendor security assessment before being granted access.

Data Sharing Agreements: Any sharing of data with third-party service providers will require a Data Processing Agreement (DPA), ensuring they adhere to the company's data security protocols and applicable data protection laws (e.g., GDPR).

External Access Monitoring: Third-party access will be limited and monitored. Contractors or vendors will receive time-bound access and can only use secure, company-provided systems to interact with sensitive data.

steps.heading: Key measures to obtain stakeholder consent

substeps.text: Consent Forms: Customers or clients must be provided with clear consent forms when collecting personal or confidential information. These forms will outline: The type of data being collected (e.g., contact information, financial data). The purpose of data processing (e.g., marketing, order processing). Data sharing policies, including whether data will be shared with third parties. The retention period for which the data will be stored. Contact details for data inquiries or requests for information deletion.

Explicit Consent: Consent must be collected through opt-in mechanisms, such as checkboxes or electronic signatures, ensuring customers provide explicit permission for their data to be collected, processed, and shared.

Privacy Policy: Customers will be informed of the company's data use policies via the Privacy Policy, which will be accessible on the company's website and during onboarding processes. The Privacy Policy must cover: Data collection practices: What data is collected, and why. Data storage and sharing practices: How and where data is stored, and if it's shared with third parties. Customer rights: Including the right to access their data, request data corrections, or delete their data.
Consent Management: Customers will have access to a consent management platform or portal, allowing them to modify their data-sharing preferences or revoke consent at any time.

steps.heading: Processing, Sharing, and Retention of Confidential Information

substeps.text: Data Minimization: The company will only collect and process the minimum amount of personal data necessary to complete the business function. Unnecessary data collection is prohibited.

Data Sharing with Third Parties: Any sharing of customer or client data with third parties must be pre-approved by the customer. The third parties will be clearly listed in the consent forms or agreements.

Data Retention: Customer data will only be stored for as long as necessary to fulfill the purpose for which it was collected. Data retention periods will be clearly communicated to customers. For example: User Data Backup: Retained for 5 years. Information Security Records: Retained for 3 years. Closed Circuit Television (CCTV): Retained for 15 days. System Access Logs: Retained for 1 year. Incident Response Reports: Retained for 2 years. Audit Logs: Retained for 3 years. Software Licensing Records: Retained for 7 years. Employee Termination Records: Retained for 2 years. Vendor and Third-Party Contracts: Retained for 6 years. Email Communications (Official): Retained for 3 years.

Customer Information Sessions: Prior to collecting data, customers will be given information sessions or online materials (e.g., webinars, tutorials) detailing the nature of the data collected and how it will be processed and stored.

Point of Contact: Customers will have a direct line to the Data Protection Officer (DPO) for queries or concerns regarding their data. The DPO can be reached at dpo@permeshwarcreations.com or via phone at 91-022-28226246.

Data Updates and Changes: If there are any changes in the way data is processed, stored, or shared, customers will be promptly notified via email or SMS and will be required to reaffirm their consent for continued data use.

Breach Notification: In case of unauthorized access or data breaches, the company will notify affected customers within 72 hours of discovering the breach, detailing: The nature of the breach. Steps taken to mitigate the breach. Recommendations for customers to secure their accounts.

Consent Records: Centralized Record Keeping: All consent forms, agreements, and any modifications to customer consent will be securely stored in a centralized database. These records will be accessible by authorized personnel only. Audit Trails: All customer interactions regarding data consent will be logged in a detailed audit trail, ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements.

Data Retention Logs: Automated Retention Monitoring: The IT team will implement automated systems to monitor data retention periods, ensuring data is deleted or archived when it reaches the end of its retention period. Review and Deletion: Any data flagged for deletion will be reviewed by the Data Compliance Team, ensuring it meets the data retention and deletion policy.

sops.title: Procedure for Managing and Disposing of Hazardous Waste

blocks.text: This SOP establishes the guidelines and procedures followed by Permeshwar Creations Pvt. Ltd. for the safe labeling, storage, handling, and transportation of hazardous materials. The primary goal is to minimize environmental impact, ensure regulatory compliance, and protect the health and safety of employees and the surrounding community.

This procedure applies to all operations at Permeshwar Creations Pvt. Ltd. involving hazardous substances used in manufacturing processes. It covers all employees, contractors, and personnel involved in production, maintenance, and management tasks related to hazardous materials.

substeps.text: Consistent Labeling: Ensure that all hazardous materials are labeled according to Globally Harmonized System (GHS) standards, including hazard symbols, risk phrases, and safety instructions. Labels must be checked and updated biannually.
Clear Communication: Labels should be in both the local language and English, ensuring they are clear and understandable for all employees.
Regular Inspections: Conduct monthly inspections to verify that labels are intact, legible, and correctly placed.
Dedicated Storage Areas: Store hazardous materials in specific, well-ventilated areas with clear signage indicating restricted access. A compliance assessment should be conducted every three months.
Secondary Containment: Use secondary containment measures (e.g., spill pallets, bunds) to prevent leaks and spills from contaminating the environment.
Environmental Controls: Implement temperature and humidity controls in storage areas to maintain safe conditions for hazardous materials. Monitor these conditions daily.
Inventory Control: Maintain an up-to-date inventory of all hazardous materials, with inventory checks conducted every 30 days to ensure accuracy.

Personal Protective Equipment (PPE): Provide appropriate PPE (e.g., gloves, goggles, respirators) to all personnel handling hazardous substances and enforce its use. PPE must be inspected weekly for wear and tear.
Employee Training: Conduct annual training sessions on safe handling practices, including emergency response procedures for spills or exposure.
Controlled Handling Areas: Restrict handling activities to designated areas with appropriate ventilation and spill containment measures.

Certified Transport Vehicles: Use vehicles certified for the transport of hazardous materials, equipped with spill response kits and proper signage. Vehicle inspections should be performed every 15 days.
Driver Certification: Ensure that drivers are trained in the safe transport of hazardous materials, including emergency response protocols. Training should be refreshed every six months.
Documentation: Ensure that all hazardous materials are accompanied by proper documentation, including Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS), transport manifests, and emergency contact details.
Safe Route Planning: Plan transportation routes to avoid populated areas and environmentally sensitive zones, reducing risks during transit. Routes should be reviewed and optimized quarterly.

steps.heading: Specialized Treatment and Safe Disposal of Hazardous Substances

substeps.text: Waste Segregation: Separate hazardous waste from non-hazardous waste at the source, with proper labeling and containment. Segregation procedures should be reviewed every two months.
Neutralization and Treatment: Apply neutralization or chemical treatment processes before disposal to reduce toxicity and environmental harm.
Waste Minimization: Implement strategies to reduce hazardous waste generation through process improvements and material substitution.
Record Keeping and Reporting: Maintain detailed records of hazardous waste disposal, including quantities, methods, and certificates of destruction. Reports should be compiled monthly.

narrative.text:
Routine Inspections: Conduct annual inspections of storage, handling, and transportation activities to ensure compliance with safety standards.
Data Analysis: Analyse incident reports, spill data, and disposal records to identify areas for improvement. Data should be reviewed annualy.
Internal Audits: Conduct annual internal audits of hazardous substances management practices, reviewing all protocols and identifying areas for enhancement.

Incident Documentation: Document all incidents involving hazardous substances, including causes, response actions, and outcomes. Documentation should be completed within 24 hours of the incident.
Response Evaluation: Evaluate response actions following each incident to identify root causes and implement corrective measures. Evaluations should be conducted within 7 days of the incident.
Corrective Action Plan: Develop and implement corrective action plans based on incident evaluations to prevent future occurrences.

sops.title: Hazardous Substances Substitution: Finding Safer Alternatives

blocks.text: This SOP outlines the procedures and initiatives undertaken by Permeshwar Creations Pvt. Ltd. to reduce the use of hazardous materials in its manufacturing processes. The goal is to minimize environmental impact, enhance workplace safety, and align with sustainable practices by substituting harmful chemicals with safer, eco-friendly alternatives.

This procedure applies to all manufacturing units and operations at Permeshwar Creations Pvt. Ltd. where hazardous substances are used. It covers all employees, contractors, and personnel involved in production, maintenance, and management tasks related to chemical processes.

rows: Rishita Fashion
Plot no. 1102, Phase III, GIDC, Vapi, Valsad, Gujarat.
PK Enterprises
C-19, Hoisery Complex, Phase II, Noida, U.P- 201301, India.

substeps.text: Material Review: Conduct a thorough review of all chemicals and substances used in the production process to identify those that are hazardous. This review should be updated every six months.
Risk Assessment: Evaluate the health and environmental risks associated with each hazardous material, focusing on its potential impact on workers and the environment.

Chemical Substitution: Replace hazardous chemicals with less harmful or non-hazardous alternatives wherever possible. Examples include: Biodegradable Surfactants: Replace traditional surfactants used in cleaning and processing with biodegradable options to reduce water pollution. Enzyme-Based Processes (Bio-Processing): Substitute chemical-based processes, such as bleaching, with enzyme-based alternatives that are gentler on fabrics and the environment. Natural Dyes: Adopt the use of plant/vegetation-based natural dyes instead of synthetic dyes, reducing the chemical load in wastewater. Green Chemistry: Encourage the use of green chemistry principles in the development of new processes and products.
Training and Awareness: Provide training to employees on the safe handling and application of alternative materials. Ensure all personnel understand the benefits of using safer alternatives.
Pilot Testing: Conduct pilot tests to ensure that the alternative materials perform effectively without compromising product quality.
Supplier Collaboration: Work closely with suppliers to source safer alternatives and ensure they meet the company's quality and safety standards.

Process Re-engineering: Re-engineer manufacturing processes to reduce the need for hazardous materials. For example, optimize dyeing processes to reduce chemical usage and improve resource efficiency.
Water and Energy Efficiency: Implement measures to reduce water and energy consumption during production, which in turn decreases the demand for chemical treatments.
Waste Minimization: Focus on minimizing waste generation by optimizing material usage and recycling process residues.

narrative.text: Regular Audits: Conduct annual audits to assess the effectiveness of the reduction strategies and ensure compliance with company policies. Performance Metrics: Track key performance indicators (KPIs) related to the reduction of hazardous materials, including the volume of chemicals replaced, environmental impact, and cost savings. Continuous Improvement: Use audit results and performance data to refine strategies and identify further opportunities for reducing hazardous material usage.

Material Substitution Records: Maintain detailed records of all substituted hazardous materials, including the alternatives used, their sources, and the rationale for substitution. Environmental Impact Reports: Prepare annual reports outlining the environmental impact of the reduction strategies, including reductions in emissions, waste, and resource consumption. Compliance Reporting: Ensure that all substitutions and process changes comply with local, national, and international environmental regulations.
